item.title: High performance Git
item.author: Programming Digest <jakub@programmingdigest.net>
item.content:encoded:
High performance Git

a few hours by Ted Nyman Git is more than version control. It's also a database, a cache, a graph walker, and a transfer protocol. Ted's book covers all those layers and what they cost in performance, from objects and history to packfiles, cloning, and transport. It's aimed at engineers who need Git to stay fast as repos and teams grow.
item.description: High performance Git

item.title: How the does Shazam work?
item.author: Programming Digest <jakub@programmingdigest.net>
item.content:encoded:
How the does Shazam work?

Shri Khalpada

8 minutes by Shri Khalpada Shazam ignores melody and lyrics entirely. Instead, it converts sound into a visual map of frequencies, then keeps only the loudest peaks, like a connect the dots picture of the song. Pairs of those peaks generate short codes that act as a fingerprint. Your phone sends those codes to a server, which finds a match across millions of songs in milliseconds by looking up each code directly rather than scanning every song one by one.
item.description: How the does Shazam work?

item.title: You can beat the binary search
item.author: Programming Digest <jakub@programmingdigest.net>
item.content:encoded:
You can beat the binary search

Daniel Lemire

7 minutes by Daniel Lemire Binary search beats linear search for large sorted arrays, but modern hardware can do even better. By splitting search ranges into quarters instead of halves and using CPU instructions that compare 16 values at once, a new approach called SIMD Quad cuts search times in half or more compared to binary search.
item.description: You can beat the binary search

item.title: The 20 software engineering laws
item.author: Programming Digest <jakub@programmingdigest.net>
item.content:encoded:
The 20 software engineering laws

Milan Milanović

25 minutes by Milan Milanović Software engineering has a set of timeless laws that explain why projects fail, teams slow down, and plans drift. These laws, some over 60 years old, are really about human nature, not technology. Adding people to late projects makes them later, work expands to fill available time, and any metric that becomes a target stops being useful. Learning these laws before a project goes wrong is far cheaper than learning them after.
item.description: The 20 software engineering laws

item.title: An AI agent just destroyed our production data
item.author: Programming Digest <jakub@programmingdigest.net>
item.content:encoded:
An AI agent just destroyed our production data

Jer Crane

10 minutes by Jer Crane An AI coding agent deleted a small business's production database and all backups with a single API call, wiping three months of customer data. The agent later admitted in writing that it broke every safety rule it had been given. Two vendors share the blame: Cursor's safety guardrails failed to stop the agent, and Railway had no confirmation step for destructive actions, no scoped API tokens, and stored backups inside the same volume they were meant to protect. item.description: An AI agent just destroyed our production data

item.title: High-performance distributed caching with .NET
item.author: C# Digest <jakub@csharpdigest.net>
item.content:encoded:
High-performance distributed caching with .NET

Jared Meade

Jared's guide walks through building a .NET console app with a two-layer caching setup using HybridCache and PostgreSQL. Slow external data calls that take seconds are replaced with responses returning in under a millisecond from memory, or in a fraction of a second from the database cache. When the in-memory cache expires, the database cache keeps things fast, and only after both expire does the app fetch fresh data from the source.
item.description: High-performance distributed caching with .NET

item.title: external APIs
item.author: C# Digest <jakub@csharpdigest.net>
item.content:encoded:
external APIs

Adrian Bailador

Adrian explains the Anti-Corruption Layer pattern in .NET, which protects your domain from being polluted by external APIs. He shows how to isolate and translate external models into your own domain language, keeping business logic clean. By using an Anti-Corruption Layer, changes in external systems only affect one layer, making your application easier to maintain, understand, and extend.
item.description: external APIs

item.title: Explore union types in C# 15
item.author: C# Digest <jakub@csharpdigest.net>
item.content:encoded:
Explore union types in C# 15

Bill Wagner

C# 15 adds union types, letting you declare a value as exactly one of a fixed set of types. The compiler enforces exhaustive pattern matching, so missing cases cause warnings at build time rather than failures at runtime. Types in a union do not need to share a common ancestor. The feature is available now in .NET 11 Preview 2 with language version set to preview.
item.description: Explore union types in C# 15

item.title: ASP.NET Core cookie size limits in production: Causes and fixes
item.author: C# Digest <jakub@csharpdigest.net>
item.content:encoded:
ASP.NET Core cookie size limits in production: Causes and fixes

Khalid Abuhakmeh

Khalid argues that authentication can fail in production due to oversized cookies. ASP.NET Core stores user claims in cookies, which can grow too large from many claims, tokens, or multiple schemes. This causes silent login failures or HTTP 431 errors. Solutions include reducing claims, disabling token storage, clearing old cookies, or using server-side sessions. The best approach is minimizing cookie data and loading user information on demand.
item.description: ASP.NET Core cookie size limits in production: Causes and fixes

item.title: Build your own CQRS dispatcher in .NET 10
item.author: C# Digest <jakub@csharpdigest.net>
item.content:encoded:
Build your own CQRS dispatcher in .NET 10

Mukesh Murugan

MediatR went commercial in July 2025, pushing many teams to find alternatives. In this article, Mukesh built a custom CQRS dispatcher in .NET 10 that replaces MediatR with about 100 lines of code, supports the same pipeline behavior pattern, returns ValueTask for fewer allocations, and benchmarks 4.4x faster than MediatR 12.4.1 on real BenchmarkDotNet runs. And the most popular article from the last issue was:
item.description: Build your own CQRS dispatcher in .NET 10

families: model-level and system-level.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Model-level defenses teach the model to resist injection.</p><ul style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;">Spotlighting wraps untrusted text in control tags like <UNTRUSTED>...</UNTRUSTED> and tells the model to treat anything inside as data, not instructions.</p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;">Instruction Hierarchy fine-tunes the model to rank the developer's system prompt above the user's message, and both above third-party content.</p></li></ul><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">System-level defenses build a system around the LLM that bounds the damage.</p><ul style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;">Least-Privilege Tools: Give the agent the minimum tools it needs.</p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;">Human-in-the-Loop: Require explicit user approval before any sensitive action runs.</p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;">Planner / Executor Split: Two separate LLMs. The planner has tool access but never sees untrusted content. The executor reads untrusted content but has no tools.</p></li></ul><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">No single defense is enough. Production systems like Gmail stack them, and together they make indirect injection manageable.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Over to you: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;">Everything starts with a Feed Request.</p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;">Next, it gathers candidate posts from two sources: Thunder (posts from accounts you follow) and Phoenix Retrieval (posts from blocked authors, and muted keywords.</p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: item.title: How To Be Direct And Strategic
item.author: Pointer <suraj@pointer.io>
item.ns0:encoded:
How To Be Direct And Strategic

Yue Zhao

"I saw an issue with a process on my team recently and brought it up directly in a team meeting a few days later. I was very direct about the problem, gave all the details, and explained how it impacted everyone. To my surprise, my manager shut it down completely, and now I cannot get any buy-in from anyone. What happened? Where did I do wrong?"

#Leadership Communication
item.description: How To Be Direct And Strategic

item.title: Drunk Post: Things I’ve Learned As A Senior Engineer
item.author: Pointer <suraj@pointer.io>
item.ns0:encoded:
Drunk Post: Things I’ve Learned As A Senior Engineer

Kirill Bobrov

“A few years ago, a data engineer got drunk and wrote down everything he learned in 10 years of engineering. The original account is deleted, but the post captures something real — the kind of honesty you only get after a few glasses of wine. Preserving it here, typos and all.”

#CareerGrowth BestPractices Entertaining
item.description: Drunk Post: Things I’ve Learned As A Senior Engineer

item.title: Speak In The Affirmative: "Do This" Versus "Don't Do That"
item.author: Pointer <suraj@pointer.io>
item.ns0:encoded:
Speak In The Affirmative: "Do This" Versus "Don't Do That"

Wes Kao

“It’s to your benefit to be as clear as possible when you speak or write, because clear communication helps you get what you need. One way to do this is to speak in the affirmative, rather than the negative... If you speak in negatives, your recipient has to take an extra mental step.”

#Leadership Management Communication
item.description: Speak In The Affirmative: "Do This" Versus "Don't Do That"

item.title: How I Use AI To Code
item.author: Pointer <suraj@pointer.io>
item.ns0:encoded:
How I Use AI To Code

Chris Parsons

A practitioner's guide to AI-assisted coding in 2026. Senior engineers should shift from reviewing AI-generated diffs to training the harness that produces them via CLAUDE.md files, skill files, and feedback loops. The bottleneck has moved from code generation to verification.

#AI Guide BestPractices
item.description: How I Use AI To Code

item.title: Structured-Prompt-Driven Development
item.author: Pointer <suraj@pointer.io>
item.ns0:encoded:
Structured-Prompt-Driven Development

“Instead of relying on ad hoc chats, SPDD turns prompts into assets that can be: version controlled, reviewed, reused, and improved over time. Teams use structured prompts to capture requirements, domain language, design intent, constraints, and a task breakdown. Then the LLM generates code within a defined boundary, so output becomes more predictable and easier to validate.”

#AI Guide BestPractices
item.description: Structured-Prompt-Driven Development

item.title: Email Is Crazy
item.author: Pointer <suraj@pointer.io>
item.ns0:encoded:
Email Is Crazy

Saurabh Khawase

“Email evolved organically over the years, tracing its origins to the academic labs of ARPANET in the ’70s. Its various components were designed by different people, at different times, facing different challenges. The email ecosystem is a very complex beast with more than 100 RFCs mandating its various protocols.” A deep dive into how email works under the hood.

#Infrastructure DeepDive
item.description: Email Is Crazy

item.title: How To Make A Fast Dynamic Language Interpreter
item.author: Pointer <suraj@pointer.io>
item.ns0:encoded:
How To Make A Fast Dynamic Language Interpreter

Fil Pizlo

“This post is about optimizing an extremely simple AST-walking interpreter for a dynamic language called Zef that I created for fun to the point where it is competitive with the likes of Lua, QuickJS, and CPython.”

#SystemDesign DeepDive
item.description: How To Make A Fast Dynamic Language Interpreter

20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;margin-top: 0;text-align: justify">Think about the difference between leaving a housemate a to-do list and writing them a contract. The to-do list says “buy bread on Monday, take out the bins Tuesday, water the plants Wednesday.”</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">It’s a sequence of instructions, and if any step fails or gets skipped, the whole thing fails. The contract says something different. It says the kitchen should always have bread, the bins should never overflow, and the plants should never go three days without water. One is a script. The other is a promise, and somebody has to keep checking whether the promise is being kept.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">Kubernetes is what we get when that second approach is taken seriously and built into a whole infrastructure platform.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">In this article, we will learn how Kubernetes is a system of promises, and that every piece of it is a small program keeping one of those promises.</p><div style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;margin-top: 0;"><em><span>Hi, this is Gergely with a bonus, free issue of the Pragmatic Engineer Newsletter. In every issue, I cover Big Tech and startups through the lens of senior engineers and engineering leaders. Today, we cover one out of three topics from </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/17d55837-434a-4828-993a-197c8eb3a4f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMzZ4bDFvIn0.YQmyE28ZLdSE7AAsuvKXIbV3t_oMMHyypLc7Hwjh0tE" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">last week’s The Pulse</a><span> issue. Full subscribers received the article below seven days ago. If you’ve been forwarded this email, you can</span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/8fb53e4d-9f43-4902-af34-56360e0ba368?j=eyJ1IjoiMzZ4bDFvIn0.YQmyE28ZLdSE7AAsuvKXIbV3t_oMMHyypLc7Hwjh0tE" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;"> subscribe here</a><span>.</span></em></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>Last week, we covered </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/d75f15f8-53fa-412e-9807-c6643dfa872a?j=eyJ1IjoiMzZ4bDFvIn0.YQmyE28ZLdSE7AAsuvKXIbV3t_oMMHyypLc7Hwjh0tE" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">the slightly perverse trend of “tokenmaxxing”</a><span> across the industry, where devs run agents with the sole aim of boosting their personal “token stats” in an effort to rank higher on internal token leaderboards, and not be seen as a Luddite who doesn’t use AI tools enough compared to peers.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">This week, I spoke with a software engineer at a large company and another at a seed-stage place. Both shared almost identical stories: at their latest all-hands, company leadership expressed concerns about the fast-rising costs of tokens. At both places, token spend has increased by ~10x in the last six months – with no signs of slowing down.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">I wanted to find out about this trend, so I talked to devs at 15 businesses. Below is what I learned about what’s happening in workplaces of all sizes. Names are anonymized.</p><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: 1.625em;">Large companies</h2><h4 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: 1.125em;">Setting the default model to a cheaper one: 10,000+ person SaaS company, offices on all continents</h4><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Inside a large SaaS company, most devs use an internal background coding tool for coding. This model defaults to Claude Sonnet, which is the cheaper Claude version. Model selection is not persisted, so devs who prefer working with Opus, for instance, must reselect it on every subsequent startup.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">This tool supports all major frontier models such as Sonnet, Opus, GPT, and Gemini. Devs at the company whom I talked to are very heavy users of the tool and have not encountered usage limitations.</p><h4 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: 1.125em;">Fintech company, US, Series D, ~8,000 people. Staff engineer:</h4><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">“The cost in token spend is off the charts – and leadership has shared this trend with us. They have not said anything beyond showing growth in spend, and mentioning that this won’t be sustainable. So, nothing specific yet, but my sense is that something will have to change. Limits or prioritizing cheaper models, cutting back on hiring? Who knows.”</p></blockquote><h4 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: 1.125em;">Infra company, US, publicly traded, ~5,000 people. Engineering Director:</h4><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><strong>“We’re monitoring but not restricting.</strong><span> We are spot checking the heaviest users, but we are seeing the business cases working out.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">We are offering some guidance on model selection - e.g., turn off the new high-effort setting in Claude. Some users are trying open source models – but open source model usage is a bottom-up initiative, not a top-down one.”</p></blockquote><h4 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: 1.125em;">Information technology, US, 10,000+ people. Director of Engineering:</h4><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">“We have already had to raise our API budget limits multiple times in April. We recently switched to a much higher-effort level for Claude, which significantly increased the cost per PR.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><strong>One reason for the cost spike is using state-of-the-art models for demanding tasks.</strong><span> We are using that high-effort setting even for fairly trivial tasks that could have been handled by much cheaper models, or even by lower-effort Claude loops. Despite a few of us pointing this out, leadership has basically said budget is not the concern right now.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>I sense that the budget increase has not been forecasted, and we’re in for a reckoning.</span><strong> </strong><span>I suspect the attitude changes once finance and other cost-conscious parts of the org realize we are spending hundreds of dollars per day, per highly-engaged developer. For now, fear of missing out and not wanting to fall behind seems to be outweighing cost discipline.”</span></p></blockquote><h4 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: 1.125em;">Games studio, US+Europe, ~5,000 people. I talk with people at startups where $1,000/month in spending is totally normal, and it’s night and day here.”</p></blockquote><h4 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: 1.125em;">Fintech company, US+Europe, late stage, ~5,000 people. Leadership encourages using AI for code review, but my team will not blindly trust AI.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">The push from AI is coming from the top. This year’s performance review had a section on AI, rating devs by how well they used AI, so this is another reason everyone just uses it as much as they can.”</p></blockquote><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: 1.625em;">Mid-sized companies</h2><h4 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: 1.125em;">SaaS industry, US, ~2,000 people. Dev Productivity Lead:</h4><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">“Model routing helped keep our costs growing less dramatically. For example, changing the default model reduced cost by 30%. This is our strategy with AI spend, summarized:</p><ul style="margin-left: 20px;margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong>Short term: spend, spend, spend!</strong><span> Experiment and use whatever models make sense.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong>Measure the impact</strong><span>. Measure key outcomes and report on spend, monthly.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong>When spend vs results diverge: adjust. </strong><span>When our spend increases dramatically, but outcomes don’t follow: see what we can do to adjust the delta. More spend should mean better outcomes. If not, we are doing something wrong.”</span></p></li></ul></blockquote><h4 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: 1.125em;">Finance industry, US, ~2,000 people. VP of AI:</h4><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">“We have Cursor and Claude Desktop, both of which have around 800-1,200 total users. Token usage is growing somewhat unexpectedly. Estimates are being adjusted on the fly; the initial plan to have strict limits (say, $100 per user) is breaking when reality hits, and people exhaust them in 3-5 working days.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Using expensive models is a problem. In regards to Cursor, many devs are defaulting to the most expensive models without realizing that going with Opus gives single percentage gains in intelligence compared to Sonnet, for example, while exhausting their budgets almost immediately.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><strong>We are working on blocking/managing out the most expensive models [with Cursor]</strong><span>, as going into thousands of dollars per user, per month is not sustainable on our scale. Cursor is a good partner and we’re working with them to switch to a “pooled spend” model where heavy users can tap into a pool of extra spend.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Claude is a similar story. We were at $100 of Claude Desktop limit for everyone, but as we are moving forward, I can see that we would need to go much higher, especially for business-critical use cases.”</p></blockquote><h4 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: 1.125em;">Infra company, US, late-stage, ~700 people. Founder:</h4><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">“We haven’t had much of an issue. Most folks police themselves for runaway costs; for example, we had someone hit like $10K in a week because they messed up caching, but it was caught and they corrected their harness.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><strong>For the most part, we don’t see our high-end folks spending more than ~$1K/week.</strong><span> Now, to be clear, this is not a small amount! BUT it’s already a small subset of the population.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">We’re just factoring it into engineering costs at this point: if it’s, say, $2K/month per employee, that’s $24K per year.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Who cares, then, when engineers already cost $200-400K/year in cash comp? Okay, so what if it’s $5K/month. That’s $60K/year.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><strong>Our bet is that token costs will stabilize and we’ll eventually end up with local-ish models.</strong></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Now, it could be five years before they stabilize, but overall, spend today isn’t that insane to me.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>There’s a lot of people who are just dumb about it, but most legit execs push back on this. Take the </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/3fe5226f-c471-464d-b885-a473ce5635a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMzZ4bDFvIn0.YQmyE28ZLdSE7AAsuvKXIbV3t_oMMHyypLc7Hwjh0tE" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">Ralph loops</a><span> or other insanity where someone spends $1K/day, $5K/week or stuff like this. That’s all just people being fools thinking they’re doing “R&D,” or somehow that they’re smarter than everyone else, but they’re just producing junk that never ships or is not useful.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><strong>We saw a bit of “stupid overspend” in the first couple months, but that’s all gone now. </strong><span>Costs could go up even more if we would “crack the whip” in wanting to see even more output, but we’re not doing that.”</span></p></blockquote><h4 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: 1.125em;">Healthcare industry, US, ~500 people. Senior engineering manager:</h4><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>“</span><strong>We are not holding back on spend, and have a monthly spend leaderboard.</strong><span> And we WANT devs to spend more on tokens! For example, one of my engineers spent $1,400 on a long Claude Code session in a single day.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><strong>We are seeing massive leverage, and we do more with the same number of people. </strong><span>This is why we are okay with our spending spiking. Our traffic is growing more than 10x, year-on-year, and we have managed to keep things running with the same team, and these AI tools.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Engineering is now blocked on Product and Design – which never happened before! This is how fast execution has become. We now have Staff+ engineers writing Product PRDs so we can move faster.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">I’ve been in tech for close to 15 years and I never saw dramatic change like this. I just came back after a 3-month break, and every single thing is different in my day! I feel these AI agents are the biggest change in the industry since high-level languages became widespread.”</p></blockquote><h4 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: 1.125em;">E-commerce company, US & Europe, ~2,000 devs. Head of Engineering:</h4><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">“The increase in spend is INSANE. It’s about usage going up, with no signs of stopping. Usage is off the charts.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">We currently do not have limits in place, and are not pausing now. Our CEO is AI-pilled and won’t let us slow down.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><strong>We do buy tokens at a discount. </strong><span>They start from 5% and go up with usage with the vendors we use (the usual suspects.)</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">We don’t let devs use anything lower than Opus 4.7 for coding. Cheaper models might work better, but a slight error pushed to prod would result in hours of toil.”</p></blockquote><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: 1.625em;">Small companies</h2><h4 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: 1.125em;">Series A, US, ~50 people. Principal Engineer:</h4><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">“About 15 devs are heavy users of AI and costs are rising very fast. Almost everyone uses Claude and Claude Code. We are considering four potential options:</p><ol style="margin-left: 20px;margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong>Increase AI budget, and start measuring more</strong><span>. Continue doing what we are, but allow devs to use more tokens instead of hiring limits. The precise ROI is hard to quantify, but we’ll start to measure and track both AI adoption and impact.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong>Optimize token consumption. </strong><span>Use cheaper models for simpler tasks, review token usage, and see where we can cut usage. Downside: this approach could become one with diminishing returns, fast.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong>Integrate more AI providers in the company.</strong><span> Find wrappers to abstract LLMs. The problem is: how do you replace Claude Code, for instance?</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong>Pivot to local models:</strong><span> such as Kimi, Qwen, and so on. The problem is it’s a big investment in high-end hardware or cloud GPUs. Upside: it offers better long-term cost control, once done.</span></p></li></ol><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">We are likely to go with option #1: increase spend BUT maintain momentum and put the right measurements in place. We can do #2, #3 and #4 later. But if we kill AI usage momentum inside the company, the outcome will probably be worse.”</p></blockquote><h4 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: 1.125em;">AI infra, US, seed stage, ~15 people. Founder:</h4><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>“</span><strong>We saw a 15x increase in 6 months:</strong></p><ul style="margin-left: 20px;margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;">Six months ago our spend per developer was ~$200/month</p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;">Today, it’s around $3,000/developer/month, for our seven devs</p></li></ul><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">We’re not slowing usage, especially as we are building an AI infra product. The increase was much faster than expected, though.”</p></blockquote><h4 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: 1.125em;">Small, bootstrapped company, Europe. Founding engineer:</h4><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #FF6B00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">“Our current strategy in dealing with the increase in costs is to switch to a cheaper model; unfortunately, from Opus to Sonnet in our case. That said, Sonnet is quite decent.”</p></blockquote><h3 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: 1.375em;">How businesses manage token spend</h3><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Regardless of company size, there seems to be two strategies for how companies deal with increased spending. A summary:</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><strong>Strategy #1: “let it rip and start measuring.” </strong><span>Around half of respondents say AI spend is rising dramatically, and they have decided to do nothing about it. They </span><em>want</em><span> devs to use AI as much as it makes sense to, and to help the work as much as possible.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">However, because the cost is rising dramatically, these companies are now starting to measure usage and attempting to measure the impact of their AI tools.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">There’s a few companies where the impact seems to be very positive, already. Smaller startups whose business is exploding in numbers of customers, load, and revenue, see that they don’t need to hire more staff because existing engineers can keep supporting the growth with AI tools.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><strong>Strategy #2: curb spending.</strong><span> Commonly mentioned cost-saving approaches:</span></p><ul style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;">Use cheaper models for simpler tasks</p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;">Set default models to less capable ones</p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;">Set a spending cap and make it hard for engineers to exceed it, or require consent for doing so</p></li></ul><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Most companies using strategy #1 have briefly considered going with this approach, but threw it away, because they see this approach as optimizing on the wrong thing: cutting costs before the productivity impact of using state-of-the-art tools is even known!</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><strong>Discounts exist when the spend is in the millions of dollars. </strong><span>I asked several people if they are getting discounts from vendors when buying tokens at scale. There were no exact numbers, but this is what I gathered in aggregate about possible custom agreements:</span></p><ul style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong>Cursor: open to discounts above a few million dollars in spend. </strong><span>Companies have negotiated discounts with Cursor after crossing $1M of spending. Some companies negotiated tiered discounts from this level, starting at 5% and going higher as their spend goes up.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong>Anthropic: no discounts. </strong><span>I talked with companies spending $5M+ per year on Claude which have received no discounts. If Anthropic offers discounts, it will likely be at a much higher tier.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong>All discounts are custom, so try to negotiate – it’s free! </strong><span>Pricing discounts are on a per-customer basis, and highly custom. The easiest way to see if a discount is available is to ask the vendors!</span></p></li></ul><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><em>—-</em></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><em><span>Read the full issue of </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/17d55837-434a-4828-993a-197c8eb3a4f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMzZ4bDFvIn0.YQmyE28ZLdSE7AAsuvKXIbV3t_oMMHyypLc7Hwjh0tE" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">last week’s The Pulse</a><span>, or check out </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/a7c4de44-793c-4e18-9e6b-f3c21cc2a72b?j=eyJ1IjoiMzZ4bDFvIn0.YQmyE28ZLdSE7AAsuvKXIbV3t_oMMHyypLc7Hwjh0tE" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">this week’s The Pulse</a><span>. This week’s issue covers:</span></em></p><ol style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;margin-bottom: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong>Load from AI breaks GitHub – but why not other vendors? </strong><span>GitHub’s reliability is less than one nine, and getting worse. Prolific open source contributor, Mitchell Hashimoto, is quitting GitHub because he thinks it’s not suited for professional work. GitHub’s leadership blames the 3.5x increase in service load as the cause of degradation – or it might be self-inflicted.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong>Anthropic’s speedrun to destroy trust.</strong><span> Anthropic could do no wrong until recently, but in the past month, that’s all changed. Silently nerfing Claude Code, banning companies from Claude, and baffling price rises all add to a sense that Anthropic is in its “extraction” era of generating more revenue for the same or worse service.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong>Industry pulse. </strong><span>Dramatic price increases at GitHub Copilot, explosive growth at Codex, Google scrambling to build a good coding model, Cursor might be bought by SpaceX, AI agent deletes car business, and more.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong>Mitchell Hashimoto & the “building block economy</strong><span>.</span><strong>” </strong><span>Ghostty’s creator finds that open source “building blocks” are the best way to win massive adoption by software components – but it’s got harder to build a business on top of open building blocks.</span></p></li></ol></div></div><div class="container-border" models. Few optimize inference. We benchmarked NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell on Akamai Cloud against H100 using real LLM workloads.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">At 100 concurrent requests, Blackwell reached 24,240 tokens/sec per server, compared to 1,863 TPS on H100. That’s up to 1.63× higher throughput, with additional gains from FP4 precision. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">The difference comes down to architecture. These GPUs run on a globally distributed platform built for real-time, latency-sensitive inference, not centralized batch jobs. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">If you're building agentic systems or high-concurrency AI apps, infrastructure choices matter as much as model selection. See the full setup, methodology, and results. View benchmark results</p><p class="button-wrapper" data-attrs="{"url":"https://go.bytebytego.com/Akamai_042926","text":"View Benchmark results","action":null,"class":null}" data-component-name="ButtonCreateButton" style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: center;cursor: pointer;border-radius: 4px;"><a class="button primary" href="https://substack.com/redirect/2429c487-b1d3-419e-8bc8-a341d6df1582?j=eyJ1IjoiMzZ4bDFvIn0.YQmyE28ZLdSE7AAsuvKXIbV3t_oMMHyypLc7Hwjh0tE" style="font-family: system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';display: inline-block;box-sizing: border-box;cursor: pointer;border: none;border-radius: 8px;font-size: 14px;line-height: 20px;font-weight: 600;text-align: center;margin: 0;opacity: 1;outline: none;white-space: nowrap;color: #ffffff !important;text-decoration: none !important;background-color: #7756e3;padding: 12px 20px;height: auto;"><span style="color: #ffffff;text-decoration: none;">View Benchmark results</span></a></p><div style="font-size: 16px;line-height: 26px;"><hr style="margin: 32px 0;padding: 0;height: 1px;background: rgb(0,0,0,.1);border: none;"></div><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">In 2024, Wise’s deployment system automatically blocked hundreds of releases that would have caused production incidents.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">There was no human intervention, but the system routed just 5% of traffic to the new version, watched technical and business metrics for 30 minutes, and rolled back when it detected anomalies. Three years earlier, Wise was deploying with a simpler in-house tool that treated each release as a basic transaction, where the process was essentially to push the code and hope for the best.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">This leap was made possible by some interesting engineering decisions that we will learn about in this article.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">For reference, Wise moves about £36 billion across borders every quarter, with 65% of transfers arriving instantly. One might assume that kind of reliability requires a tightly controlled, top-down engineering organization. However, the opposite is true.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">Wise has 850+ engineers organized into autonomous squads, each empowered to make their own technical decisions. The reason this works, and the reason it would collapse without a very specific set of infrastructure investments, is the real engineering story behind Wise.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">Behind the product that 15.6 million active customers interact with, there are over 1000 microservices, 700+ Java repositories, 40 web applications, and native iOS and Android apps with hundreds of modules each. What holds all of this together is an internal platform, a set of shared tools, frameworks, and automated systems that make the right engineering choice the easy one.</p><div justify"><em>Disclaimer: This post is based on publicly shared details from the Wise Engineering Team. Please comment if you notice any inaccuracies.</em></p><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: 1.625em;text-align: justify">Standardizing the Starting Point</h2><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">When a system has 1000+ services owned by dozens of independent teams, the most dangerous form of complexity is inconsistency. If every team wires up security, database connections, Kafka consumers, and logging differently, you end up with 1000 slightly different systems that are all hard to debug, upgrade, and secure.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">Wise’s answer to this is a microservice chassis framework, an opinionated, pre-configured foundation that every new backend service can start from. The chassis handles security, observability, database communication, Kafka integration, and more, all with recommended defaults so that teams can focus on business logic rather than plumbing.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">What makes Wise’s approach distinct is that the chassis is shipped as a versioned artifact rather than a template you fork and modify.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">The difference matters. With a template, the service diverges from the standard the moment you create it. With an artifact dependency, updates to the chassis flow downstream when teams bump the version. Security patches, observability improvements, and new defaults reach services through a regular dependency upgrade rather than a manual migration.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">This approach also extends to the build pipeline.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">Wise built a collection of in-house Gradle plugins, including one that standardizes GitHub Actions workflows. When Wise decided to roll out SLSA (a framework for protecting software supply-chain integrity) across the organization, it became a plugin version update across 700+ Java repositories rather than 700 individual pull requests.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">On top of this, a language-agnostic automation service can make complex changes across the codebase at scale and create pull requests for the owning team to review. Dependency upgrades for Java services are now fully automated through this system.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">The same standardization mindset shows up on the frontend.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">Wise’s web applications are built on CRAB, a Wise-specific abstraction on top of Next.js, split across 40 distinct apps that handle specific product functions. Visual regression testing is handled by Storybook paired with Chromatic, which captures snapshots of React components after each change and highlights visual differences to catch UI bugs before they reach customers.</p><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: 1.625em;text-align: justify">Shipping Code Safely</h2><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">Standardizing how services are built is only half the problem. The other half is standardizing how they reach production.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">Since 2018, Wise has relied on Kubernetes to host its services, originally built with Terraform, JSONNET, and ConcourseCI. That setup supported service-mesh controls through Envoy, PCI-DSS compliance, and frictionless deployments for several years.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">But as Wise grew, the original approach could not scale further without becoming a maintenance burden. This led to the Compute Runtime Platform (CRP), a ground-up rebuild of Wise’s Kubernetes infrastructure. Terraform still provisions infrastructure, but the codebase was rewritten from scratch for flexibility. RKE2 now handles cluster bootstrapping, with Rancher managing overall cluster state. Helm replaced JSONNET for better maintainability and upstream compatibility. ArgoCD with custom plugins ensures fully automated provisioning and consistency across environments. The result is that Wise grew from 6 Kubernetes clusters to more than 20 while keeping maintenance manageable.</p><div class="captioned-image-container-static" style="font-size: 16px;line-height: style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;text-align: justify">Automated container CPU rightsizing through Vertical Pod Autoscaler is now live in non-production and rolling out to production for non-critical workloads.</p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;text-align: justify">Horizontal scaling through KEDA optimizes workloads based on daily and weekly traffic patterns.</p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;text-align: justify">Fully managed sidecar containers like the Envoy proxy simplify deployments for product teams, and Wise’s Envoy-powered service proxy now includes seamless integration and discovery between services.</p></li></ul><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">All of this feeds into Wise’s broader Mission Zero cost optimization goals.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">Wise’s deployment strategy has undergone a big shift with the transition from Octopus, their former in-house tool, to Spinnaker. This was more than a tool swap.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">Octopus treats deployments as simple transactions, while Spinnaker treats them as orchestrated sequences of events with built-in canary analysis, metric validation, and automatic rollback.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">See the diagram below:</p><div class="captioned-image-container-static" style="font-size: 16px;line-height: 26px;margin: 32px auto;"><figure style="width: canary process is simple in concept but powerful in practice.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">When a new version of a service is deployed, only 5% of traffic routes to it. Over a 30-minute window, the system analyzes both technical metrics (error rates, latency) and business metrics (transaction success rates, conversion). If it detects significant anomalies, it rolls back automatically. In 2024, this system prevented hundreds of potentially incident-causing deployments and saved thousands of engineering hours. Over half of Wise’s services already run on Spinnaker, with full migration expected by mid-2025.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">On the CI side, migrating from CircleCI to GitHub Actions opened new optimization possibilities. By tracking detailed build metrics, Wise discovered that pre-populating caches for frequently used containers could slash build times by 15%. At their scale of 500,000 monthly builds, that translates to over 1,000 hours saved each month. Wise has also been methodically implementing the SLSA framework across build processes, strengthening supply-chain security one language at a time.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">Mobile teams have seen similar gains.</p><ul style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;text-align: justify">iOS engineers migrated 250+ Xcode modules from Xcodegen to Tuist and switched from Cocoapods to Swift Package Manager, dropping zero-change build times from 28 seconds to 2 seconds.</p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;text-align: justify">On Android, the team manages over 300 Gradle modules and has fully moved to Jetpack Compose for UI, adopted Kotlin 2.0 and 2.1, and is exploring Kotlin Multiplatform for cross-platform code sharing.</p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;text-align: justify">Backend-for-frontend services (BFFs, which are lightweight backends tailored to a specific frontend’s needs) help share logic between Android, iOS, and web teams.</p></li></ul><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: 1.625em;text-align: justify">Connecting to Payment Rails</h2><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">Fast, safe deployments matter even more at Wise than at most companies, because what those services are doing is moving real money through real banking systems around the world.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">Wise connects directly to local payment schemes rather than routing through intermediary banks. They went live with InstaPay in the Philippines, were granted access to Zengin (Japan’s instant payments system), and received access to PIX in Brazil. Each of these integrations has different technical requirements, and some demand a physical data center presence in the country.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">This creates an infrastructure consistency challenge.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">Wise centralizes networking using AWS Transit Gateways, but the details of each integration vary substantially across their UK, Hungary, and Australia data center deployments. The Australian deployment is particularly interesting because it was one of the first deployments of AWS Outpost Servers, which allowed Wise to maintain consistent AWS tooling even inside a physical data center.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">The goal is always to keep the infrastructure as uniform as possible so that teams working on payment integrations can focus on the business logic rather than wrestling with environment differences.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">Wise also exposes this infrastructure through a public API, allowing banks, financial institutions, and enterprises to integrate cross-border payment services directly. For reference, the Wise Platform supports over 40 currencies and multiple payment routes, with OAuth authentication and built-in compliance features.</p><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: 1.625em;text-align: justify">Data, ML, and AI</h2><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">All of this money movement generates enormous volumes of data. Wise’s data architecture is built as a pipeline from movement to insight to action, with each layer feeding the next.</p><div class="captioned-image-container-static" style="font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">Kafka underpins most of Wise’s real-time data movement, handling asynchronous messaging between services, log collection, and streaming updates for analytics. Their Kafka clusters have grown significantly, with features like rack-aware standby replicas for fault tolerance.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">An in-house data movement service funnels information from Kafka and databases into destinations like Snowflake, S3 Parquet, and Apache Iceberg, with automated checks in the configuration process to reduce human error.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">A separate Data Archives service now handles over 100 billion records across multiple databases, reducing storage costs and making backups faster.</p><h3 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: 1.375em;text-align: justify">Storing and Querying Data</h3><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">Wise has migrated most MariaDB and Postgres workloads from self-hosted EC2 instances to Amazon RDS, and is moving from self-hosted MongoDB to MongoDB Atlas. using Apache Iceberg, which allows modifying table structures without rewriting all the data. Trino serves as the federated query engine, letting teams query Iceberg tables, Snowflake, or Kafka streams from one place. A Trino gateway handles workload separation and fault-tolerant queries, while Airflow and dbt-core manage complex data workflows.</p><h3 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: 1.375em;text-align: justify">Data Governance</h3><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">Wise has built a comprehensive inventory system and governance portal that tracks where data is stored, who created it, and how it is classified.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">Automated data discovery feeds into data deletion, compliance, and audit initiatives. For a regulated financial services company, this is load-bearing infrastructure, and as more engineers join the governance effort, Wise is rolling out stricter policies, enhanced privacy checks, and automated data lifecycle management.</p><h3 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: 1.375em;text-align: justify">Machine Learning</h3><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">Data scientists work in Amazon SageMaker Studio, with large-scale processing on Spark in EMR and orchestration through Airflow.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify">SageMaker Feature Store keeps hundreds of features in sync for training and inference, while MLflow tracks experiments, metrics, and model versions.
